titulo: Airbus Delays Development of Hydrogen-Powered Aircraft

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: European manufacturer Airbus has announced a delay in its development efforts of a hydrogen-powered aircraft. The company explained that progress on the project has been slower and more complex than expected.

Airbus had set a goal to make a zero-emission airplane by 2035. The company has not announced a new target date for the plane’s production. But the French union Force Ouvrière said some of its aircraft workers were recently told the technology was running five to 10 years behind, Reuters news agency reported.
The French news agency AFP reported Airbus also said it had reduced the program’s budget by 25 percent, but was still examining ways to reduce emissions.
Airbus noted it has no plans to completely stop developing hydrogen-powered aircraft technology. The company said it sees hydrogen as “a revolutionary energy source for aviation."

However, Airbus said in a statement to Reuters it recognizes that developing systems to produce, transport, and store hydrogen represent “a huge challenge requiring global collaboration and investment."
However, much of the hydrogen used for fuel is produced using natural gas or coal. Both of these production methods often release carbon dioxide gas, which can warm the atmosphere.

Running renewable electricity through water can produce hydrogen without adding to carbon emissions. However, this process is generally more costly. Transporting and storing hydrogen also present problems.

As a gas at room temperature, hydrogen takes up a very large space. This makes it impossible to use as fuel. It first needs to be turned into a liquid to be transported or stored. And it needs to be cooled to -253° Celsius to be liquefied. This cooling process requires its own source of energy. Liquified hydrogen still takes up four times the space of jet fuel.

The airline industry trade association IATA believes aviation will reach most of its reduction in emissions by using sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). It believes other technologies, like hydrogen, will take longer to develop.
SAF uses food and plant waste from cities, agricultural and forest wastes, and other non-petroleum sources. This fuel is then added to jet fuel in mixtures of 10 to 50 percent to become SAF.
titulo_es: Airbus delays development of its hydrogen-powered aircraft
resumen_es: Airbus postpones its project for a zero-emission hydrogen-powered aircraft and cuts its budget; the text explains the difficulties of producing, transporting and storing hydrogen and the industry’s bet on sustainable aviation fuels (SAF).
nivel_motivo: The technical vocabulary (liquefied, emissions, petroleum) raises the calculated level, but the sentences are clear and the text is short, so it corresponds to B2.

ideas_clave.idea: Airbus has postponed its hydrogen aircraft project, originally due by 2035, because progress has been slower and harder than foreseen; workers were told it is five to ten years behind.
The company has cut the programme's budget by a quarter but does not intend to abandon hydrogen, which it still regards as revolutionary for aviation.
Airbus admits that building systems to produce, move and store hydrogen requires worldwide cooperation and funding.
Most hydrogen is currently made from fossil fuels that emit carbon dioxide, while clean production from renewable electricity is more expensive.
Hydrogen must be cooled to -253°C to become liquid, which consumes energy, and even then it needs four times more space than conventional jet fuel.
The industry body IATA expects most emission cuts to come from sustainable aviation fuel, made from waste and blended with kerosene, rather than from hydrogen.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that Airbus has delayed its plan to build a zero-emission, hydrogen-powered aircraft by 2035, since the project has proved slower and more complex than expected. Although the company has reduced the programme's budget by a quarter, it insists that it will not abandon hydrogen. The main obstacles are clear: most hydrogen is still produced from fossil fuels, clean alternatives are costly, and the gas must be cooled to extremely low temperatures and still occupies far more space than jet fuel. Consequently, the airline association IATA expects sustainable aviation fuel to deliver most emission cuts.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Airbus has announced that its hydrogen-powered plane will now be ready in 2040.
preguntas.cita: The company has not announced a new target date for the plane’s production.
preguntas.explicacion: Airbus has not announced a new date. The delay of five to ten years comes from what a union says workers were told.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the French union Force Ouvrière, how far behind is the technology?
preguntas.cita: the technology was running five to 10 years behind
preguntas.explicacion: The union speaks of a delay of five to ten years. The other figures do not appear in the text.

preguntas.pregunta: By how much has Airbus reduced the program's budget?
preguntas.cita: it had reduced the program’s budget by 25 percent
preguntas.explicacion: According to AFP, the cut is 25 %. The 10 % and 50 % figures are the SAF blending percentages in the last paragraph.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Airbus still considers hydrogen a revolutionary energy source for aviation.
preguntas.cita: The company said it sees hydrogen as “a revolutionary energy source for aviation."
preguntas.explicacion: Despite the delay, the company keeps that assessment and does not intend to abandon the technology.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Airbus has asked the European Union for public funding to continue the project.
preguntas.explicacion: Airbus talks about the need for global cooperation and investment, but the text does not mention any request for funds from the EU.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is hydrogen produced from natural gas or coal a problem?
opciones: Because it often releases carbon dioxide
Because it takes up less space
respuestas: Because it often releases carbon dioxide
preguntas.cita: Both of these production methods often release carbon dioxide gas, which can warm the atmosphere.
preguntas.explicacion: The problem is CO2 emissions. The high cost is attributed to the method using renewable electricity, and liquefaction and volume are dealt with in another paragraph.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 6 a word that means “expensive”.
preguntas.cita: However, this process is generally more costly.
preguntas.explicacion: “Costly” is a synonym of “expensive”; although it ends in -ly, it is an adjective, not an adverb.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Once liquefied, hydrogen takes up the same space as jet fuel.
preguntas.cita: Liquified hydrogen still takes up four times the space of jet fuel.
preguntas.explicacion: Even when liquefied, hydrogen takes up four times more space than jet fuel.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 7 a verb that means “turned into a liquid”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a verb meaning 'turned into a liquid'.
preguntas.cita: it needs to be cooled to -253° Celsius to be liquefied
preguntas.explicacion: “Liquefied” is the past participle of “to liquefy”. The text also uses the variant “Liquified” as an adjective.

preguntas.pregunta: Explain why storing and transporting hydrogen is so difficult.
respuestas: As a gas, hydrogen occupies too much space, so it must be liquefied by cooling it to -253°C, which itself requires energy; even in liquid form it still needs four times as much space as jet fuel.
preguntas.cita: As a gas at room temperature, hydrogen takes up a very large space.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must cover the volume of the gas, the need to cool it to -253 °C with the energy cost that this involves, and the volume it still takes up once liquefied.

preguntas.pregunta: According to IATA, how will aviation achieve most of its emission reductions?
opciones: By reducing the number of flights
preguntas.cita: aviation will reach most of its reduction in emissions by using sustainable aviation fuel (SAF)
preguntas.explicacion: IATA relies mainly on SAF and thinks hydrogen will take longer. Reducing flights and electric aircraft are not mentioned.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 9 a word that means “combinations of several substances”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'combinations of different substances'.
preguntas.cita: This fuel is then added to jet fuel in mixtures of 10 to 50 percent to become SAF.
preguntas.explicacion: “Mixtures” are combinations of substances (es: mezclas); the industry also uses “blends”.

preguntas.pregunta: Why might sustainable aviation fuel be a more realistic short-term option than hydrogen?
respuestas: Because SAF is made from waste and other non-petroleum sources and can simply be blended with existing jet fuel, whereas hydrogen requires new, costly systems for production, liquefaction and storage that will take longer to develop.
preguntas.cita: It believes other technologies, like hydrogen, will take longer to develop.
preguntas.explicacion: An inference question: SAF is mixed with current fuel without changing the infrastructure, whereas hydrogen requires new and expensive systems.
